kibbo.eyebrow: Case Study · B2B SaaS · Built via Eleven · 2026
kibbo.title: KIBBO
kibbo.subtitle: A working hospital-equipment platform, and the website it never had.
kibbo.problem: KIBBO is a management platform (CMMS) for hospital medical equipment. The product worked, but kibbo.io still ran an old WordPress site that didn't explain it and throttled search crawlers. A biomedical engineer had nowhere to understand KIBBO, see it running, or check who already uses it.
kibbo.role: Through Eleven, I led design, front-end development, SEO/GEO and the English edition. The build ran on our AI-agent pipeline, with my review and sign-off at every checkpoint.

decisions.title: Write to the technician, not the buyer.
decisions.body: Third person, no hype, every claim shown on a real product screen, because the reader is the one who will run it every day.

decisions.title: Keep KIBBO and LEEX apart.
decisions.body: The hardware maker's figures are credited to LEEX, so KIBBO stands as its own product and never claims what it can't back.

decisions.title: Give mobile its own system.
decisions.body: "Expediente" reads each page like a case file instead of squeezing the desktop scroll into a phone.

decisions.title: Make English a real edition.
decisions.body: Own slugs, reciprocal hreflang and an untouched Spanish canonical; user quotes stay verbatim in Spanish with a labelled translation, so no one is misquoted.

kibbo.result: Live on kibbo.io in Spanish and English, replacing the legacy WordPress, with GA4 measuring from launch.
seo_items: JSON-LD: Organization, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage; ratings only where shown.
Reciprocal ES/EN hreflang, x-default and a canonical per language.
Sitemap built from one route registry, dated by real edits.
Citable guides: CMMS explainer, tender checklist, country records (ES).

leex.eyebrow: Case Study · Internal B2B System · LEEX · 2026
leex.title: LEEX Tender System
leex.subtitle: Finds public tenders across 33 sources and helps sales decide which to bid.
leex.problem: LEEX, an Argentine medical equipment company, sells mainly through public tenders: demand isn't generated, it's detected across dozens of government portals, each with its own format and deadlines. Seeing a tender late means never having it; seeing it without knowing if you qualify means losing it. The previous tool was a single-user script feeding a spreadsheet.
leex.role: I led it end to end: scoped it with sales and management, designed the architecture, and built the engine and web app with a pipeline of AI coding agents under my direction.

decisions.title: Code before AI.
decisions.body: A deterministic dictionary-plus-vector match filters first and a Claude model judges only what survives, because that keeps it cheap, testable and explainable.

decisions.title: A person signs every verdict.
decisions.body: The model drafts a requirement-by-requirement case citing the tender and the product sheet, and sales decides, because a missed tender costs far more than a review.

decisions.title: Three sweep states, not two.
decisions.body: "Nothing there", "couldn't see" and "saw far less than usual", because the expensive failure is the silent one.

decisions.title: Public first.
decisions.body: The engine reads each portal's public view and logs in only as a documented last resort, which cut credential exposure and let the build start without waiting on access.

leex.result: Running internally on real data: the first full pass went from sweep to triage to human-signed verdicts. Next step: onboarding the sales team.

b6_story.title: Where the incubator came from
b6_story.caption: In 1878, a Paris obstetrician had a zoo's poultry incubator adapted for babies; premature mortality fell from 66% to 38% with controlled heat alone. Today that idea is LEEX's B6.

kibbo_film.title: Preventive maintenance, from plan to execution
kibbo_film.caption: The maintenance plan takes a week to build, but the first surprise pulls schedule and staff apart. KIBBO puts every preventive task in one filterable list the whole team can see.

v8v_cpr.title: One button to resuscitate
v8v_cpr.caption: How long does a hospital bed take to be ready for resuscitation? On LEEX's V8v electric bed, one button: press it and the bed goes fully flat, ready for CPR, because in a cardiac arrest there's no time to lose.

mri_explainer.title: How an MRI works
mri_explainer.caption: No cameras, no X-rays: your body is full of water, and every hydrogen nucleus is a tiny magnet. A huge magnet, a radio pulse tuned to their rhythm and gradient coils turn that signal into an image. It's not a photo; it's the hydrogen in your body, made visible.

model_comparison.title: Same prompt, three models
model_comparison.caption: One prompt, three models (Sonnet 5, Opus 5.5 and Astra 6): a 3D gummy citrus slice you can stretch and twist. Real, side-by-side recordings show how each result behaves, alongside the time and tokens each model took.

items.description: Founded and operate an AI-native digital agency. 38-agent coordinated pipeline — discovery, strategy, brand, dev, QA. 4 products live in production. AI-generated digital content for clients.

Corrective and preventive maintenance of biomedical equipment at Sanatorio Allende (JCI accreditation process). Sectors: adult ICU/CCU, OR, pediatric ICU, NICU, endoscopy, wards, outpatient.
